text: The office wants to know whether a rewritten renewal message works. A seeded random number generator picks 5,000 permit holders for the rewritten message; another 5,000, picked the same way, get the standard one. On-time renewal is compared between the two groups.
Eight branch managers volunteered to install a queue kiosk in spring. By autumn the average wait in their branches is 6 minutes shorter than in the 16 branches without a kiosk.

Market stalls under 10 square metres pay no inspection fee; larger stalls pay it. An analyst compares on-time renewal among stalls of 9.0 to 9.9 square metres with stalls of 10.0 to 10.9 square metres.

Online booking was switched on in the six northern branches in June and nowhere else. An analyst compares the change in missed appointments from May to July in the northern branches with the change over the same months in the 18 other branches.
A survey of 2,000 permit holders finds that 81% of those who use the office's mobile app renewed on time, against 58% of those who do not use it.

The office has 400 fast-track inspection slots and 1,900 applicants. A recorded lottery allocates the slots. Days from application to permit are compared between applicants who won a slot and those who did not.
